options.A: so that neighbouring countries can be in-range for fixed stations.

options.D: the repeater can transmit both modes simultaneously.

options.A: time difference between the two stations prevented them both being on-air at the same time.
options.B: satellite was not accessible from both stations at the same time.
options.C: USA was too far way and the signals too weak to be heard.
options.D: two stations were using incompatible satellite prediction programs.

questions.question_text: What is the main reason for setting the transmit power to the minimum required to maintain contact?

options.A: Reduce the area over which other amateurs will suffer blocking.
options.B: Minimise the likelihood of causing interference to other electronic devices.
options.C: Optimise the signal level into the distant demodulator for clear readability.
options.D: Avoid running the final amplifier near the limit of its specification

questions.question_text: What Electromagnetic (EMC) safety precautions are essential when installing amateur radio equipment in a motor vehicle?

options.A: Connection of the radio DC supply directly to the battery with suitably rated fuses in both the positive and negative wires.
options.B: Testing to prove the absence of interference between the radio equipment and any of the vehicle's electronic systems.
options.C: Confirmation that the grounding of the feeder screen to the vehicle body at the aerial is being properly achieved.
options.D: Listening to the radio receiver whilst the engine, heater and wiper motor are running to assess how well the suppression of electrical noise produced by the vehicle is being achieved.

questions.question_text: If a complaint is made to the BBC by a neighbour about interference to their television which is then forwarded to Ofcom for action, it is likely that as a first step

options.A: you will be asked to keep a log of your transmissions and the neighbour will be asked to keep a record of instances of interference.
options.B: you will receive an immediate station inspection to check you are operating in accordance with your licence and the powers, frequencies and modes you are using.
options.C: you will receive an instruction by hand or in the mail to cease operating for a specified period of time.
options.D: you will receive a formal note of revocation of your licence giving you a period of one month to make representations to Ofcom.

questions.question_text: When might it be appropriate to disconnect the mains earth wire inside a 3-pin mains plug?

options.A: If RF is getting back into the mains from a transmitter.
options.B: When connecting it to a local RF earth.
options.C: When the power is supplied by overhead cables.

questions.question_text: What is the important advantage of using an RCBO rather than just relying on a fuse?

options.A: An RCBO will also notice human contact with Live and Neutral at the same time avoiding the risk of fatal injury.
options.B: An RCBO will detect a small current of around 30mA from live to earth but a fuse will only detect excessive currents of typically several amps.
options.C: An RCBO can be reset after it has been triggered but a blown fuse must be replaced by a new one which might not be immediately available.
options.D: An RCBO is much more accurate at detecting excessive currents but a fuse might not blow until the current is double it specified rating.

options.B: To minimise the risk of damage to the equipment.
options.C: To minimise the risk of electric shock.
options.D: To simplify the process of adjusting sensitive components.

questions.question_text: Before using an electric drill it is important to

options.B: check the chuck key has been removed.
options.D: ensure the work is properly earthed.

questions.question_text: When transmitting from a stationary vehicle it is essential to consider

options.A: the need to give your location correct to within 5km.
options.B: whether pedestrians might be inside the EMF compliance distance.
options.C: the possibility that passengers' voices may also be transmitted.
options.D: the risk of interference from the vehicle's ignition system.

questions.question_text: An Intermediate licence holder in England would have a callsign with the prefix
questions.explanation: Intermediate licence holders in England are issued callsigns with the 2E1 prefix. Foundation holders get 2E0, and Full licence holders get M0 or G callsigns.

questions.question_text: A Welsh Intermediate licence holder would use the callsign prefix
questions.explanation: Welsh Intermediate licence holders use the 2W1 prefix. 2E1 is England, GW is a Full licence Welsh prefix.

questions.question_text: A Scottish Foundation licence holder would use the callsign prefix
questions.explanation: Scottish Foundation licence holders use 2M0. GM/MM are Full licence prefixes. There is no GS prefix in amateur radio.

questions.question_text: The maximum power output permitted for an Intermediate licence holder is
questions.explanation: Intermediate licence holders are limited to 50 watts PEP. Foundation is 10W, and Full licence is 400W.

questions.question_text: The 2.4GHz ISM band overlaps with which amateur band?
questions.explanation: The 13cm amateur band (2300-2450 MHz) overlaps with the 2.4GHz ISM band used by Wi-Fi and microwave ovens. Amateurs must accept interference from ISM devices in this shared band.

questions.question_text: Two resistors of 100Ω and 200Ω are connected in parallel. The combined resistance is
A frequency of 145.500MHz is in the
questions.explanation: The 2m band covers 144-146 MHz. 145.500 MHz is the FM calling frequency on the 2m band.

questions.question_text: The wavelength of a signal at 7.1MHz is approximately
questions.explanation: Wavelength = 300 / frequency(MHz) = 300 / 7.1 = 42.25m. The 40m band is named for its approximate wavelength, but the actual wavelength at 7.1MHz is closer to 42m.

questions.question_text: According to the Nyquist theorem, a 4kHz audio signal must be sampled at a minimum rate of
questions.explanation: The Nyquist theorem states that the sampling rate must be at least twice the highest frequency in the signal. For a 4kHz signal: 2 × 4kHz = 8kHz minimum sampling rate.

questions.question_text: At resonance, a series tuned circuit has
questions.explanation: At resonance in a series tuned circuit, the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel out, leaving only the resistance. This gives minimum impedance and maximum current flow.

questions.question_text: A Field Effect Transistor (FET) has three terminals called
questions.explanation: A FET has gate, drain, and source terminals. Base/collector/emitter are bipolar transistor terminals. Anode/cathode are diode or valve terminals.

questions.question_text: If the turns ratio of a transformer is 3:1 (primary:secondary), and the input voltage is 240V AC, the output voltage will be approximately
questions.explanation: For a transformer, Vout = Vin × (Ns/Np) = 240 × (1/3) = 80V. A 3:1 step-down transformer reduces the voltage by a factor of 3.

questions.question_text: The abbreviation PLL stands for
questions.explanation: PLL stands for Phase Locked Loop, a feedback control system used in radio equipment to generate stable frequencies and for frequency synthesis.

questions.question_text: In an SSB transmitter, the unwanted sideband is removed by
questions.explanation: In an SSB transmitter, a crystal (or mechanical) filter removes the unwanted sideband from the DSB signal produced by the balanced modulator. The filter's sharp frequency response allows only one sideband to pass.

questions.question_text: The IF (Intermediate Frequency) in a superhet receiver is

options.A: always higher than the received signal.
options.B: a fixed frequency lower than the received signal.
options.C: the same as the received signal.
options.D: variable depending on the received signal.

questions.explanation: The IF in a superhet receiver is a fixed frequency, usually lower than the received signal. The local oscillator mixes with the incoming signal to produce this constant IF, making amplification and filtering easier.

questions.question_text: The characteristic impedance of most coaxial cable used in amateur radio is
questions.explanation: Most amateur radio coaxial cable has a characteristic impedance of 50Ω. 75Ω coax is used for TV aerial connections. 300Ω is typical of balanced ribbon feeder.

questions.question_text: The radiation pattern of a half-wave dipole in the plane of the antenna is
questions.explanation: In the plane of the antenna (E-plane), a half-wave dipole has a figure-of-eight radiation pattern with nulls off the ends and maximum radiation broadside to the antenna.

questions.question_text: The abbreviation MUF stands for
questions.explanation: MUF stands for Maximum Usable Frequency — the highest frequency that can be reflected back to earth by the ionosphere for a given path. Above the MUF, signals pass through the ionosphere into space.

questions.question_text: The abbreviation EMC stands for
questions.explanation: EMC stands for Electromagnetic Compatibility — the ability of electronic equipment to function satisfactorily in its electromagnetic environment without introducing intolerable electromagnetic disturbances.

questions.question_text: The Q-code QRZ means
questions.explanation: QRZ means 'Who is calling me?' It is commonly used on amateur radio to ask stations to identify themselves. QRT means closing down, QRO means increase power, QRM means interference.

questions.question_text: The Q-code QSL means
questions.explanation: QSL means 'I acknowledge receipt' or 'Can you acknowledge receipt?' QSL cards are sent between amateurs to confirm a contact. QSY means changing frequency, QRS means send more slowly.

questions.question_text: A transmitter has a power output of 50W. Expressed in dBW this is approximately
An antenna has a gain of 6dBd. Compared to the transmitter power, the effective radiated power in the main beam direction is approximately
questions.explanation: 6dB represents a power ratio of 4:1. Each 3dB doubles the power, so 6dB = 2 × 2 = 4 times the power. The ERP in the main beam is 4 times the transmitter power.

questions.question_text: The EMF compliance limit for average EIRP from an Intermediate licence holder's station is
questions.explanation: The EMF compliance limit for Intermediate licence holders is 10 watts average EIRP with a peak EIRP limit of 100 watts. Above these limits, an EMF assessment must be carried out.

questions.question_text: The unit of capacitance is the
questions.explanation: The Farad (F) is the unit of capacitance. The Henry is inductance, the Ohm is resistance/impedance, and the Coulomb is electric charge.
